title: Tipping Point: Quantized KV Failure Modes & Eval Patch Notes
body:
Context / TL;DR:
- During the afternoon rollout of the kv4b packing patch (canary on dedicated pool), we saw intermittent sequence duplication and degraded coherency for multi-turn chat workloads. Symptoms only reproduced when micro-batch size > 8 and when inference switched between 8-bit runtime path and 4-bit packing path within a single session (canary == mixed-precision fallback).
- Short term mitigation: pin offending customers to 8-bit path and revert mixed-precision routing; longer term: deterministic KV replay harness + alignment fix landed in local branch.

What happened (observable symptoms):
- Users reported mirrored tokens (token i == token i-1) in ~0.3% of responses for a small subset of prompts (system prompts with long prefix ~1.2k tokens).
- P99 latency spiked ~18% under micro-batching with default batcher windows; throughputs appeared normal.
- pToken duplication only when model used kv-prefetch + quantized 4-bit forward kernels.
- Repro steps (dev env): run bench/stream-chat --model test-l3-16k --pack-mode kv4b --batch-size 12 --seed 17 --prefix-length 1200. Intermittent dup seen in ~1/250 runs.

Diagnosis notes (what we traced):
1) KV indexing alignment: packing/protobuf alignment mismatched eviction pointer when packed_kv_size mod 32 != 0. This produced stale KV slices being read back into the cache when fallback occurred.
2) Race with async eviction thread: when micro-batcher drains and triggers early eviction while a 4-bit consolidation job is running, region lock ordering allowed a reader to observe partially-consolidated KV (partial write).
3) Rare serialization bug in packer metadata header (endian flag) — triggered only on a specific toolchain (GCC 11 / CUDA 12.0) and with opt-level -O3 inlining.

Immediate fixes attempted and results:
- Reverted mixed-precision routing for canary pool: resolved customer reports within 2 hours.
- Added a mutex around the consolidation+eviction critical region (hotfix branch: runtime/kv/lock-fix-APR12). Reduced incidence to 0 in synthetic replay for 10k runs.
- Forced packer to emit explicit alignment padding (patch in branch packing/align-explicit-APR12). Repro no longer seen in local tests.

Risk / rollback plan:
- Hotfix mutex increases contention slightly. Measured impact in staging: throughput drop ~3% at 99th percentile batch sizes; acceptable for short cooldown. If we see >5% regression, revert and keep pinned routing while we ship full fix.

New evals added (high level):
- evals/kv-integrity-replay-v1: deterministic runner that replays recorded prefixes (2.4k diverse prompts) across pack/unpack codepaths and flags deviations.
- evals/instr-follow-regression-suite: 1,200 instruction-following prompts to detect micro-regressions (metrics: pass@1, instruction-F1). Observed small regression after initial packer change: F1 delta -3.2% on a subset of templated instruction prompts.
- smoke: run evals/kv-integrity-replay-v1 across every model-onboard (staging) before flip to 4-bit.

What we learned about onboarding process:
- Onboarding checklist missed: "run kv-integrity-replay" as gating step for models with >1M KV slots and mixed routing enabled. Adding this as a required step in model-onboard checklist.
- Need to add toolchain matrix CI step: compile with GCC 11/CUDA 12 to catch packer endian/local-alignment regressions.

Open action items (owner / ETA):
- Add kv-integrity-replay to model-onboard gating (owner: Arjun) — ETA: 2026-04-18.
- Merge packing/align-explicit-APR12 and release canary build (owner: Lena) — ETA: 2026-04-15 (in review).
- Perf smoke in dedicated staging after mutex hotfix (owner: Owen) — ETA: 2026-04-14; measure p99 and throughput.
- Add toolchain CI matrix entry (owner: Maya) — ETA: 2026-04-22.
- Post-mortem doc (owner: Maya + Arjun) — ETA: 2026-04-20 (include timeline, play-by-play, and customer comms).

Short notes from today's standup (bullet capture):
- Arjun: reproduced partial-write case locally; shipping replay harness to CI.
- Lena: packing alignment patch under QA; found similar endian flag in old packer file-format tests.
- Owen: perf regressions minimal in staging, but need longer soak.
- Product: notify affected customers, offer capacity pinning and SLA credit if they hit errors.

Customer impact & comms:
- Two customers hit visible duplication; we proactively opened support tickets and offered a pinned route to 8-bit. No data loss or PII exposure.
- Comms draft in support: short description, mitigation steps, ETA for full fix, and follow-up post-mortem. (PRD-ish note: ensure legal is ok with wording.)

Quick debugging checklist (for on-call or rotation):
- If duplicate tokens reported: check runtime logs for pack-mode and batch-size, grep for "kv-consolidation-start" and "kv-evict-complete" timestamps.
- Run local replay harness with the customer prefix; if repro, escalate to eng-applied-ml bench channel and tag Arjun.
- If immediate mitigation needed: switch route to model@8bit by toggling routing policy in console (Route -> Edit -> Force model variant).

Notes to self / unresolved questions:
- Why did the toolchain specific behavior surface now? Hypothesis: new microbatch default changed on canary fleet which combined with GCC11-inlined code to expose the header endian drop. Need a small synthetic compile-time unit test to force different inlining.
- Consider switching packer serialization to an explicit versioned header with CRC to detect partial writes on read. That will make future debugging easier.

References / links:
- GH PR with hotfix + tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4821
- Jira: INF-1297 (kv packer failure triage)
- Slack trace: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C02ABC3/p1649876543210

Appendix: quick reproduction command (dev):
- docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/work:ro redwood/bench:dev-20260412 
  bench/stream-chat --model test-l3-16k --pack-mode kv4b --batch-size 12 --seed 17 --prefix-length 1200 --replay-seed 42

Status: this doc is a working capture of the incident, focusing on technical root cause and immediate mitigation. Will convert to formal post-mortem after the post-mortem meeting on 2026-04-20.

-- Maya
